web_title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain, Manufacturing & Unit Economics
book_title: Chapter 3: The Forest-to-Factory Pipeline and Unit Economics
question: How does Manorama procure wild seasonal seeds across two continents, convert them inside Birkoni, and lock in 26% operating margins—and what does every ₹100 of FY26 revenue actually earn?

epigraph.quote: Amateurs talk strategy; professionals talk procurement windows and inventory turns.
epigraph.author: Specialty Lipid Processing Maxim

web_blocks.html: Palm-oil refiners can buy crude palm oil on spot markets all year. Manorama cannot [6, 7]. Its edge—and its working-capital load—starts on forest floors [6, 7]. In India, tribal collectors gather wild sal seeds across Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Madhya Pradesh before the monsoon [5, 21]. Mango kernels arrive during the summer fruit season [5, 21]. In West Africa, shea nuts are harvested from November to February, with early buying peaking into September [7, 21]. Thousands of village aggregators, tribal co-ops, and women's groups handle collection [5, 16].

To protect seed quality and meet European traceability rules, Manorama set up its own West African arms [16]. It runs Manorama Africa Limited in Tema, Ghana, and Manorama Savannah Agro Chad SARL in Chad [16]. In Burkina Faso, it formed Taang Kaam Industries SA to process shea nuts and mango kernels locally, backed by 2026 QIP funds [16, 22]. In Brazil, Manorama Latin America LTDA teamed up with DEKEL Agroindústria in São Paulo to make CBE near South American plants [16].

web_blocks.title: The Birkoni Integrated Complex & 3–5 Year OEM Qualification Moat

web_blocks.html: Dried kernels and crude shea butter travel to the Birkoni Industrial Area complex near Raipur [2, 5]. Processing runs through four stages [2, 5, 23]. First, 90,000 MTPA of seed milling and solvent extraction separates crude fat from meal [2]. Second, a 45,000 MTPA refinery and interesterification block removes odor, color, and free fatty acids [2, 23]. Third, 47,500 MTPA of solvent fractionation (up from 40,000 MTPA via a March 2026 debottlenecking) separates hard stearin from liquid olein [5, 23]. Fourth, a 30,000 MTPA packing line fills export drums, flexitanks, and cartons [5].

Manorama sells 100% B2B to global food and beauty brands, with no retail label [14, 19]. Winning a vendor slot at Ferrero, Mondelēz, Nestlé, or L'Oréal takes a 3-to-5-year audit [19, 21]. Buyers run lab stability checks, pilot line trials, bloom tests, and village ESG audits [19, 21]. Because CBE is a small part of a chocolate bar's cost, Tier-1 buyers rarely switch suppliers once qualified [19].

web_blocks.title: Pricing Mechanics & FY26 Unit Economics Waterfall

web_blocks.html: Manorama prices CBE and specialty fats on a cost-plus conversion spread [19]. It locks in seed costs during harvest and signs 6-to-12-month supply deals that protect EBITDA per tonne [19]. In FY26, consolidated sales reached ₹1,367 Cr against ₹1,005 Cr of operating expenses [1]. That left ₹361 Cr in operating EBITDA (26.4% margin) and ₹225 Cr in net profit (16.5% margin) [1]. Debtor days fell from 48 to 17, while payable days rose from 14 to 46 [1]. Together, those shifts drove ₹250 Cr of operating cash flow [1].

web_blocks.html: Seasonal buying creates a clear half-year rhythm on the balance sheet. Inventory climbs sharply in the September quarter—reaching roughly ₹1,000 Cr during early shea and sal buying [21]. Processing and shipping through March then turn that stock back into cash [21]. In FY26, that H2 unwind cut inventory days from 518 to 369 and lifted free cash flow to ₹196 Cr [1]. Management also used ₹150 Cr from the mid-2026 QIP to pare cash-credit debt [22]. That equity buffer lowers interest drag ahead of the next ₹460 Cr capex cycle [22].

web_blocks.title: THE SEASONAL WORKING CAPITAL TRADE-OFF
paragraphs: Sal, mango, and shea harvests happen once a year, while chocolate plants run all year. Manorama must hold 369 to 518 days of inventory [1]. That stock buffer blocks small rivals who lack credit, yet it strains cash flow during rapid growth years [6, 7].

book_paragraphs: If you want to know why no well-funded startup can replicate Manorama Industries in eighteen months, follow a single tonne of shea nuts and sal seeds from the ground to a Ferrero tempering tank. It is a logistical obstacle course that punishes anyone without patience, working capital, and local roots.

Twice a year, Manorama's procurement engine goes into overdrive. Between May and July in central India, tribal collectors gather fallen sal seeds from forest floors and mango kernels from juice and pulp processors. Between November and February—and into early-season buying across the September quarter—aggregators in Ghana, Burkina Faso, and Chad collect sun-dried shea nuts from rural women's cooperatives. Miss those narrow harvest windows, and your factory sits idle for the rest of the year.

To control quality and traceability at the source, Manorama didn't rely on trading brokers. It incorporated Manorama Africa Limited in Tema, Ghana, set up Taang Kaam Industries in Burkina Faso to process nuts locally, and established Manorama Savannah Agro in Chad—even partnering with DEKEL Agroindústria in São Paulo, Brazil, to serve Latin American confectioners directly.

book_subsections.title: Inside Birkoni: Four Stages of Value Addition
paragraphs: Once dried seeds and crude shea butter reach Birkoni, Chhattisgarh, they enter a four-stage industrial machine. First, 90,000 MTPA of seed milling and solvent extraction strips crude exotic fat from the meal. Second, a 45,000 MTPA refinery and interesterification block removes free fatty acids, gums, and odors. Third—the crown jewel—a 47,500 MTPA solvent fractionation complex, expanded in April 2024 and debottlenecked by 7,500 MTPA in March 2026, uses precision temperature-controlled crystallization to separate symmetric stearin triglycerides from liquid olein. Fourth, a 30,000 MTPA packing line prepares export drums, flexitanks, and carton blocks.

Even with a world-class plant, you cannot simply knock on Mondelēz or Hershey's door and start shipping. Global food and beauty giants run 3-to-5-year qualification audits—testing fat crystallization, chocolate snap, heat resistance, and village-level ESG traceability. Once you pass, however, you are embedded in their global recipe.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Look at the FY26 unit economics waterfall: out of every ₹100 of sales (₹1,367 crore total), ₹73.52 covered all operating costs, leaving ₹26.41 in EBITDA and ₹16.46 in net profit. Even better, after years of negative CFO, FY26 converted ₹18.29 per ₹100 of sales into ₹250 crore of operating cash flow—proving the Birkoni economics work at scale when inventory turns smoothly.

book_subsections.title: Cost-Plus Contracts and the Working-Capital Trade-Off
paragraphs: How does Manorama protect those 26% operating margins when soft-commodity prices swing wildly? By pricing CBE and specialty-fat contracts on a cost-plus conversion spread. Management locks in raw seed prices during the harvest window and signs 6-to-12-month forward customer contracts calibrated to preserve absolute EBITDA per metric tonne.

Meanwhile, payment terms tightened noticeably in FY26: debtor days fell from 48 days in FY25 to just 17 days, while payable days expanded from 14 to 46 days. That combination—fast collections from Tier-1 multinationals plus 369 days of raw-seed buffer—slashed the cash conversion cycle from 552 days to 340 days and generated ₹196 crore of free cash flow in FY26.

book_subsections.title: The Seasonal Cash Rubber-Band: Why March and September Look Different
paragraphs: If you want to understand Manorama's balance sheet without getting blindsided in October, you have to understand the forest calendar. In central and eastern India, sal seeds and mango kernels drop onto the forest floor in a frantic six-to-eight-week window between April and June, right before the monsoon rains arrive and spoil the crop. In West Africa, the shea nut harvest concentrates between June and September. If Manorama waited to buy seeds only when a chocolate customer placed a monthly order, there would be no seeds left to buy.

So Manorama acts as a seasonal sponge. Through thousands of village-level aggregators and self-help groups in Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Madhya Pradesh—and through its own subsidiaries in Burkina Faso, Togo, Benin, and Ghana—the company buys an entire year's worth of raw seeds in cash during those peak collection months. That is why inventory days sit at 369 days in FY26 (down from 518 days in FY25, yet still a full year of stock) and why short-term working-capital borrowings surge every September before liquidating back down by March as finished CBE is shipped out.

Walk through the FY26 ₹100 cash waterfall with that lens. Out of every ₹100 of revenue on FY26's ₹1,367 crore top line, ₹73.52 goes to raw seeds, chemicals, power, and operating expenses, leaving ₹26.41 in operating EBITDA. After ₹1.90 in depreciation, ₹2.78 in interest, ₹0.73 in other income, and ₹6.07 in tax, ₹16.46 drops to net profit. Crucially, because receivable days tightened from 48 to 17 days and payable terms stretched from 14 to 46 days, FY26 converted ₹18.29 per ₹100 of revenue into operating cash flow—funding ₹3.95 of capex and still leaving ₹14.34 per ₹100 in free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Inside Birkoni: Seed Milling, Refining, and 47,500 MTPA Fractionation
paragraphs: To appreciate the engineering barrier inside Manorama's plant, trace a batch of raw kernels through the Birkoni complex. First comes mechanical cleaning and seed milling across 90,000 MTPA of capacity, followed by solvent extraction to pull crude fat from the crushed meal—leaving behind protein-rich de-oiled cake sold to animal-feed buyers. Next, the 45,000 MTPA refinery strips out free fatty acids, gums, and color bodies so the oil meets food-grade purity.

The real crown jewel is the final stage: 47,500 MTPA of fractionation capacity (expanded by 7,500 MTPA through debottlenecking completed in March 2026), backed by 30,000 MTPA of specialized packing. Here, controlled crystallization separates liquid olein from solid stearin at precise melting points. That single technical step—repeated reliably across thousands of tonnes—is what transforms a ₹90-per-kilo crude forest oil into a high-margin functional ingredient.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Manorama's inventory days—518 days in FY25, improving to 369 days in FY26—would terrify a traditional FMCG analyst. Here, a deep raw-seed buffer is the price of admission to run a continuous 365-day specialty refinery.
